# Building A2 — roof diaphragm shears and shear wall loads for wind

You are the delegated engineer for the **lateral package** of Building A2 at the Northern Divide
Data Campus, in Lewis and Clark County, Montana: a single-storey data hall with a steel roof deck
on joists and girders, carried laterally by precast concrete wall panels acting as shear walls on
every exterior building line, with a parapet cantilevering above the roof deck.

Your job is to work out **how the wind gets from the wall panels into the roof deck diaphragm and
back out into the shear walls**, to design the deck, the chords and collectors and the panel
connections that carry it, and to hand over the package the Engineer of Record will check: plan
drawings of the diaphragm unit shears and the shear wall loads, the schedules behind them, and a
calculation package.

The building is not the clean rectangle the 2024 drawings show. The as-built geometry is in the
2026 federated model and the roof line scan.

## What you are given

The task folder (project/, library/ and templates/) is the document set issued for this package: the structural design criteria, the
boundary-layer wind study and its coefficient data, the topographic study, the AHJ letter, the
survey and the roof line scan, the 2026 federated model, the architectural and structural
drawings, the precast panel drawings and schedule, the deck, chord and connection catalogues, the
owner's basis of design, the submittal specification, and the public standards library. It also
holds superseded revisions and a study of a different building on the same campus; part of the
job is knowing which document governs.

Nothing has been pre-digested for you. Every parameter you need is in those files — including the
analysis procedure the criteria requires you to use, and the verification example it publishes so
you can check your implementation before you trust it.

## What you must deliver

Write **`output/submission.zip`** containing exactly these five files (blank templates for the two
workbooks and the drawing are in `templates/`):

**1. `lateral_schedule.xlsx`** — nine worksheets.

* `DeckZones`: one row per deck zone —
  `zone_id, deck_code, G_prime_used_kip_per_in, capacity_asd_plf, area_sf, cost_usd`.
  `G_prime_used_kip_per_in` is the shear stiffness you actually used for that zone and
  `capacity_asd_plf` the shear capacity you checked against.
* `ChordSchedule`: one row per chord and collector line — `chord_id, section_code, length_ft,
  cost_usd`.
* `Piers`: one row per pier — `pier_id, panel, line, s0_ft, s1_ft, width_ft, thickness_in,
  top_z_ft, k_kip_per_in, embeds, tiedown`. `s0_ft`/`s1_ft` are the pier's extent along its wall
  line, `top_z_ft` the top of that panel, `k_kip_per_in` the stiffness you assigned it, `embeds`
  the number of deck-to-panel embeds on that panel and `tiedown` `yes` or `no`.
* `ShearWalls`: one row per wind scenario per wall line — `scenario, line, line_load_plf,
  reaction_kips`. `line_load_plf` is the roof-level line load on that wall line and
  `reaction_kips` the load that wall line takes out of the diaphragm. Report unit shears, line
  loads, reactions, chord forces and deflections as **magnitudes**; the scenario already says
  which way the wind blows, and either sign convention is read the same way.
* `Diaphragm`: one row per wind scenario, wall line and report station — `scenario, line,
  station_frac, unit_shear_plf`. The criteria fixes which stations are reported; use those.
* `Chords`: one row per wind scenario per chord and collector line — `scenario, chord_id,
  force_kips`.
* `Drift`: one row per wind scenario per global axis — `scenario, direction, deflection_in`.
* `Convergence`: one row per mesh refinement level — `level, mesh_size_ft, elements,
  max_unit_shear_plf, key_reaction_kips`, with `key_reaction_kips` the reaction of wall line W in
  scenario W01.
* `Cost`: `item, quantity, unit_cost_usd, total_usd`, one row per cost item, summing to the
  installed cost of the package.

**2. `diaphragm_plan.dxf`** — the plan view drawings, on the building grid in feet, with the
layers and the content the submittal specification requires.

**3. `constraint_register.xlsx`** — sheet `Register`, columns
`document, clause, requirement, value, units, items`: the requirements you applied, where each
one comes from, the value it sets, and the items it binds.

**4. `calculations.pdf`** — the calculation package, in the format and with the sections the
criteria and the submittal specification require.

**5. `design_basis.md`** — the design basis narrative, carrying the two tables the submittal
specification defines and, in prose, every conflict between issued documents that you resolved
and how.

## How it is graded

Per wind scenario: the package must be present and parseable; every constraint family is checked;
and the objective credit is the ratio of a certified cost bound to your installed cost, paid only
when you miss no hard family.

    score = 0.4 * p + 0.6 * [h = 1] * O

where `p` is the fraction of the 36 constraint families you both satisfied **and** registered, `h`
is the fraction of the 22 hard families you both satisfied and registered (`[h = 1]` is 1 when all
22 are, else 0), and `O` is the objective credit (at most 1). A hard miss zeroes the `O` term. The
score is the mean over a held-out subset of the twelve wind scenarios. Constraint families cover
the set-out and take-off from the as-built geometry, the deck, chord, collector and connection
design, the acceptance limits, the agreement of every reported quantity with the Engineer's
re-analysis of **your** design, and the design basis.

**The register is scored.** A family counts only when the requirements that govern it appear in
your register, matched on document and clause. So the rules, in full:

* one document per row, at most three clauses and at most eight numbers in a row;
* a row citing a document that is not in the corpus, or a clause that does not appear in the
  document it cites, or a number that contradicts that clause, is a **wrong row**;
* a row citing a **superseded** revision or another building's study is a wrong row;
* a row that cites a genuine clause this register does not happen to index is **neutral** — it
  neither helps nor hurts, so documenting more of the corpus than is asked for is never punished;
* precision is `1 - wrong / claimed`, and **a register whose precision falls below 0.60 is
  voided entirely** — every family then counts as unregistered. At most 150 rows are judged.

## Working notes

Write a first COMPLETE version of `output/submission.zip` early and improve it in place: the last
version on disk when the run ends is what gets graded, and an imperfect early package earns
partial credit while no package earns none.

Your workspace has Python 3 with numpy, scipy, openpyxl, ezdxf, reportlab, pdfplumber and pymupdf already installed. There is no network access, so pip cannot install anything else.

## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · Lewis and Clark County, Montana · Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC · Revision 2, 14
August 2026 · supersedes Revision 0 of 3 May 2024
1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
collector forces, deflections - is an ALLOWABLE STRESS DESIGN quantity, obtained from the strength-level
wind effect by the load combination 0.6W. Member and connection capacities are compared against it on the
same basis. The drawings and the calculation package must state on their face that the loads shown are ASD.
4. Wind parameters
4.1 Exposure Category C, open terrain, in all directions. Enclosure classification: enclosed, GCpi = ±0.18. Internal
pressure acts on opposite internal faces simultaneously and therefore cancels in the net lateral force on the main wind
force resisting system; it is not to be included in the diaphragm and shear wall loads. It is included in the out-of-plane
panel design, which is a separate submittal.
4.2 The velocity pressure at elevation z is
    q(z) = 0.00256 * Kz(z) * Kzt * Kd * Ke * V^2      [psf, V in mph]
    Kz(z) = 2.01 * (z / 900)^(2/9.5),  z not taken less than 15 ft
with Kd = 0.85 and V from the AHJ letter. q_h is q(z) evaluated at the mean roof height; the velocity pressure for a
parapet is evaluated at the top of that parapet.
4.3 The topographic factor Kzt is taken from the site-specific study TS-2026-02 and applies over the whole footprint.
Revision 0 of this criteria carried Kzt = 1.00 and a basic wind speed of 105 mph; both were superseded when
the topographic study and the AHJ letter were issued.
4.4 The ground elevation factor is
    Ke = exp(-0.0000362 * zg)      zg = site ground elevation above sea level, ft
with zg taken from the ALTA survey benchmark. Ke is not to be taken as 1.0 at this site.

--- Page 2 ---

5. Precast wall panels
5.1 The perimeter walls are precast concrete panels spanning vertically between the foundation and the roof deck, with
a parapet cantilevering above the deck. Panel-to-panel joints transfer no in-plane shear: each panel resists in-plane
force independently.
5.2 Panel concrete f'c = 5000 psi, Ec = 4030 ksi, G = 0.40 Ec, unit weight 150 pcf.
5.3 Panel geometry - mark, length, thickness, top elevation and openings - is taken from the as-built federated model
and the roof line scan. Where the 2024 precast panel schedule and the as-built model disagree, the as-built model
governs and the difference is to be reported in the design basis.
5.4 Openings divide a panel into vertical legs. A leg is the full-height strip of panel between an opening edge and the
next opening edge or panel edge. A leg narrower than 2.0 ft is neglected: it is assigned no stiffness and carries no
in-plane shear.
5.5 Each leg is idealised as a cantilever pier fixed at the foundation and free at the roof deck, of height h equal to the
roof deck elevation, with
    k = 1 / ( h^3 / (3 Ec I) + 1.2 h / (G A) )        [kip/in]
    I = t L^3 / 12,   A = t L,   t = panel thickness, L = leg length
with h, t and L in inches. The parapet above the deck contributes no in-plane stiffness.
5.6 A panel's in-plane shear is the sum of the shears of its legs.
5.7 The panel base connection to the foundation has the ASD shear capacity per foot of panel length given in the
connection vendor data; the demand is the panel's in-plane shear.
5.8 Panel stability is checked with the ASD combination 0.6D + 0.6W: the overturning moment is the panel's ASD
in-plane shear times the roof deck elevation, and the resisting moment is 0.6 times the panel self weight times half the
panel length. Where the resisting moment is insufficient, a base tie-down assembly is provided; the assembly's ASD
capacity acts at a lever arm equal to the panel length. Panel self weight is computed on the GROSS panel area - full
panel length by top elevation by thickness - with no deduction for openings.
6. Wind pressures and the roof-level wall line load
6.1 The wind study reports a pressure coefficient for each facade patch and each azimuth, referenced to q_h. The
design pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp. The net pressure on a parapet patch is p = q_p * GCpn, with q_p the

page 3
velocity pressure at the top of that parapet and GCpn the study's net parapet coefficient; the parapet coefficient already
includes both faces.
6.2 Patch geometry is not tabulated in the wind study. A patch covers the full length of the panel it names and the
elevation band its identifier names; the bands are defined in the wind study. Panel lengths and top elevations come
from the as-built model.
6.3 Wall pressures act on the gross wall area, including door and louver openings; the door and louver framing delivers
its reaction to the surrounding panel.
6.4 Each panel spans vertically as a simple beam between the foundation and the roof deck. A patch pressure
p acting on an area A whose centroid is at elevation z therefore delivers
    R_roof = p * A * z / h        to the roof deck, and
    R_base = p * A * (1 - z/h)    to the foundation
with h the roof deck elevation. A patch above the deck - a parapet or a screen wall - has z > h, so it delivers
MORE than its own force to the diaphragm and an uplift-sense reaction at the base: this is the lever action of
the wall cantilevering above the diaphragm and it is not to be omitted. The roof-level line load on a wall line is the
sum of R_roof over the patches of that line, per foot of wall.
6.5 The line load acts along the wall's inward normal.
6.6 Torsional case. For wind on either principal axis the diaphragm is also checked with all line loads factored by 0.75
together with a torsional moment
    M_T = e * B * |F|        e = +/- 0.15
where |F| is the magnitude of the factored resultant in the direction of the wind and B the horizontal building dimension
perpendicular to the wind (240 ft for wind on the north or south face, 180 ft for wind on the east or west face). M_T is
applied to the diaphragm as a set of in-plane nodal forces proportional to the nodal tributary area and to the distance
from the diaphragm area centroid, directed perpendicular to that radius, scaled so that their moment about the centroid
equals M_T.
7. Roof deck
7.1 The roof is divided into the deck zones shown on S-201. Exactly one deck type from the deck manufacturer's
catalogue is used over the whole of each zone.
7.2 The diaphragm unit shear anywhere within a zone must not exceed the ASD shear capacity of that zone's deck
type. The catalogue tabulates NOMINAL strengths; the safety factor for the ASD capacity is given in the catalogue's
notes.
7.3 The catalogue's shear stiffness G' is tabulated for the deck span stated in its notes; where the framing gives a
different deck span, the note's adjustment applies. The adjustment applies to stiffness only, never to strength.
8. Acceptance limits
8.1 All checks are on the ASD basis of 3.3.
8.2 Diaphragm deflection. For each scenario and each global axis, the deflection of the diaphragm relative to its
supports is the largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from the stiffness-weighted mean displacement of the
piers that resist that axis. It must not exceed 0.55 in, the value the Owner's Basis of Design sets for the precast
connection detail.
8.3 Pier drift must not exceed h / 400.
9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this building. T

    R_base = p * A * (1 - z/h)    to the foundation
with h the roof deck elevation. A patch above the deck - a parapet or a screen wall - has z > h, so it delivers
MORE than its own force to the diaphragm and an uplift-sense reaction at the base: this is the lever action of
the wall cantilevering above the diaphragm and it is not to be omitted. The roof-level line load on a wall line is the
sum of R_roof over the patches of that line, per foot of wall.
6.5 The line load acts along the wall's inward normal.
6.6 Torsional case. For wind on either principal axis the diaphragm is also checked with all line loads factored by 0.75
together with a torsional moment
    M_T = e * B * |F|        e = +/- 0.15
where |F| is the magnitude of the factored resultant in the direction of the wind and B the horizontal building dimension
perpendicular to the wind (240 ft for wind on the north or south face, 180 ft for wind on the east or west face). M_T is
applied to the diaphragm as a set of in-plane nodal forces proportional to the nodal tributary area and to the distance
from the diaphragm area centroid, directed perpendicular to that radius, scaled so that their moment about the centroid
equals M_T.
7. Roof deck
7.1 The roof is divided into the deck zones shown on S-201. Exactly one deck type from the deck manufacturer's
catalogue is used over the whole of each zone.
7.2 The diaphragm unit shear anywhere within a zone must not exceed the ASD shear capacity of that zone's deck
type. The catalogue tabulates NOMINAL strengths; the safety factor for the ASD capacity is given in the catalogue's
notes.
7.3 The catalogue's shear stiffness G' is tabulated for the deck span stated in its notes; where the framing gives a
different deck span, the note's adjustment applies. The adjustment applies to stiffness only, never to strength.
8. Acceptance limits
8.1 All checks are on the ASD basis of 3.3.
8.2 Diaphragm deflection. For each scenario and each global axis, the deflection of the diaphragm relative to its
supports is the largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from the stiffness-weighted mean displacement of the
piers that resist that axis. It must not exceed 0.55 in, the value the Owner's Basis of Design sets for the precast
connection detail.
8.3 Pier drift must not exceed h / 400.
9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this building. The following semi-rigid model is required, and the submitted
quantities are checked against it.

=== Page 4 ===
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 4
9.1 Mesh. A structured square mesh of side H is laid over the bounding rectangle of the roof, with its origin at the
building grid origin. A cell belongs to the diaphragm when its centre lies inside the roof outline and outside a roof
opening. Nodes are the corners of the cells that belong. Refinement levels: L1 H = 10.0 ft, L2 H = 5.0 ft, L3 H = 2.50 ft.
9.2 Elements. Each cell is a four-node bilinear membrane integrated with 2 x 2 Gauss quadrature, carrying the stress
resultants
    Nx  = EAx * eps_x        Ny = EAy * eps_y        Nxy = Ghat * gamma
    Ghat = 12 * G'           [kip/ft, with G' in kip/in]
EAx and EAy are the smeared axial rigidity of the roof framing, in kips per foot of width, computed as the chord area of
the member divided by its spacing times Es = 29,000 ksi - the girders east-west and the joists north-south, both from
the framing plan and the joist schedule. The deck itself is not credited with axial rigidity.
9.3 Chords and collectors are two-node bar elements of area A and Es = 29,000 ksi on the lines of section 10, one
bar per mesh interval, acting in the direction of the line.
9.4 Supports. Each pier of 5.5 is a spring of stiffness k acting in the plane of its wall, attached at the mesh node
nearest the mid-point of the leg. Where two piers resolve to the same node their stiffnesses add.
9.5 Loads. The roof-level line load of 6.4 is applied to the perimeter nodes of its wall line as the consistent nodal loads
of the piecewise-linear hat functions between adjacent nodes on that line.
9.6 Recovery. The diaphragm unit shear of an element is Ghat times the engineering shear strain at the element
centre. The unit shear reported at a station on a wall line is that of the element which has an edge on that wall line and
whose centre is nearest the station. A wall line's reaction is the sum of its piers' spring forces. A chord or collector force
is the largest bar force on that line.
9.7 Mesh convergence. The model is run at all three levels. The convergence measure is the relative change between
L2 and L3 in the reaction of wall line W under scenario W01, which must not exceed 5 %. The largest unit shear in the
building is a corner quantity and does not converge at that rate; report it at each level, but do not use it as the
convergence measure. Level L2 is the level at which the submitted quantities are reported and checked.
9.8 Verification example VE-1
An implementation of DIAPH-MT must reproduce the following before it is applied to Building A2. A rectangular
diaphragm 100 ft (east-west) by 60 ft (north-south), mesh H = 5.0 ft, one deck type with G' = 30.0 kip/in everywhere (no
span adjustment), EAx = 2,900 and EAy = 13,920 kip/ft, chord bars of A = 3.00 in² on all four edges, and twelve piers
each of k = 500 kip/in: four on the y = 0 line and four on the y = 60 line at x = 12.5, 37.5, 62.5 and 87.5 ft resisting X,
and two on the x = 0 line and two on the x = 100 line at y = 15 and 45 ft resisting Y. Loads: a uniform inward line load of
0.50 kip/ft on the y = 0 line and 0.30 kip/ft on the y = 60 line, both at strength level, no torsional case.

10. Chords and collectors
10.1 Chord and collector lines are shown on S-201 and are listed there with their identifiers. Every line carries a section

=== DOCX: OBD-NDDC-A2_Owners_Basis_of_Design_extract.docx ===
OBD-NDDC-A2 Owner's Basis of Design (extract)
Northern Divide Infrastructure LLC - Owner's Basis of Design, Building A2. Extract of section 4, Structure. Revision 3, 2 July 2026.
4.1 Structural system
Single-storey data hall with a steel roof deck on open-web joists and girders, carried laterally by precast concrete perimeter wall panels acting as shear walls on all exterior building lines.
4.2 Service life
50 years design service life. No change of occupancy is contemplated.
4.3 Roof access
The mechanical yard on the north elevation is screened; the screen wall is part of the precast panel and extends above the roof deck. Roof access is by the north-east stair only.
4.4 Deflection and movement
The precast connection detail adopted for this campus tolerates a roof diaphragm deflection relative to its supports of 0.55 in. The structural design criteria applies this as a limit for every wind scenario and both global axes.
4.5 Deck finish
Deck is to be primed; acoustic deck is not required in the data halls.
4.6 Trade standardisation
To hold the erection, inspection and quality-assurance programme to one mobilisation per trade, not more than 4 distinct roof deck types (gauge, support fastener pattern and sidelap connection count taken together) may be used across the Building A2 roof.
4.7 Cost cap
The installed cost of the lateral package - roof deck, chords and collectors, deck-to-panel embeds and panel base tie-downs - is capped at $310,000. Costs are taken from the rates in the issued catalogues and the chord steel rate of $2.85 per pound installed.
4.8 Commissioning
Not applicable to the structural package.

import numpy as np

# VE-1 parameters:
# 100 ft (EW) by 60 ft (NS), H = 5.0 ft
Lx, Ly, H = 100.0, 60.0, 5.0
nx, ny = int(Lx / H), int(Ly / H)
# Nodes: (nx+1) x (ny+1)
# Let node index be ix * (ny+1) + iy or iy * (nx+1) + ix
def nid(ix, iy):
    return iy * (nx + 1) + ix

n_nodes = (nx + 1) * (ny + 1)
ndof = 2 * n_nodes
K = np.zeros((ndof, ndof))
F = np.zeros(ndof)

# Work in feet and kips (displacements in feet, stiffness in kip/ft)
G_prime = 30.0 # kip/in
Ghat = 12.0 * G_prime # 360 kip/ft
EAx = 2900.0 # kip/ft
EAy = 13920.0 # kip/ft
D = np.diag([EAx, EAy, Ghat])

# 4-node bilinear square element of side H x H
# For a square of side H x H, Jacobian J = diag(H/2, H/2), detJ = H^2 / 4, invJ = diag(2/H, 2/H)
gp = 1.0 / np.sqrt(3.0)
gauss_pts = [(-gp, -gp), (gp, -gp), (gp, gp), (-gp, gp)]
Ke = np.zeros((8, 8))
for xi, eta in gauss_pts:
    # N1 = 0.25*(1-xi)*(1-eta), N2 = 0.25*(1+xi)*(1-eta), N3 = 0.25*(1+xi)*(1+eta), N4 = 0.25*(1-xi)*(1+eta)
    dN_dxi  = 0.25 * np.array([-(1-eta),  (1-eta), (1+eta), -(1+eta)])
    dN_deta = 0.25 * np.array([-(1-xi),  -(1+xi),  (1+xi),   (1-xi)])
    dN_dx = dN_dxi * (2.0 / H)
    dN_dy = dN_deta * (2.0 / H)
    B = np.zeros((3, 8))
    for a in range(4):
        B[0, 2*a]   = dN_dx[a]
        B[1, 2*a+1] = dN_dy[a]

\1\ 
Description of changes: 
This update to UFC 3-301-01 incorporates a change to Tsunami design provisions 
wherein “other utilities”, which would generally refer to elements of secondary or tertiary 
importance, may be designed for a reduced risk category where approved by the AHJ.  
Additionally, an existing prohibition against the use of fabric hangar doors in windborne 
debris regions has been changed to include fabric covered buildings in general in 
windborne debris regions. 
Reason for changes: 
Regarding tsunami design change:  In some cases it may be infeasible to harden all 
elements of a utility system against tsunami effects, particularly less critical distributions 
systems.  Accordingly, it was decided that the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) can 
approve the reduction of tsunami risk category for “other utilities”, which can have the 
effect of reducing or eliminating tsunami design requirements for secondary and/or 
tertiary systems. 
Regarding fabric covered buildings in windborne debris regions:  It became apparent that 
there was an omission in DoD structural criteria, wherein an existing prohibition against 
the use of fabric covered hangar doors existed, while there was no such prohibition 
against using fabric covered buildings in general, which are vulnerable to the same failure 
mode.  Moreover, this omission would result in a prohibition against the use of a fabric 
door on a fabric covered building, which would prove illogical.  Awareness of this omission 
occurred as a result of a recent emphasis on the utilization of fabric covered buildings 
across the Department of Defense.  Fabric, unlike other construction materials is uniquely 
vulnerable to tearing and tear propagation do to windborne debris.  Past experience with 
Hurricane Michael at Tyndall Air Force Base has demonstrated this vulnerability.   
Impact:  There are both costs and benefits to these changes 
Tsunami design changes:  This change will result in substantial cost savings to the 
Department of Defense over time, where the department is impacted by tsunami.  
Fabric covered structures:  A direct increase in cost will be negligible for this change, as 
the life cycle cost for a fabric covered building, compared to a metal clad building, will not 
vary significantly for windborne debris regions.  Ultimately however, it is expected that 
this prohibition will result in considerable savings to DoD, by reducing facility loss and 
facility content loss due to damage caused by major hurricanes and typhoons.

Description of changes (seismic coefficients): 
Seismic design values for OCONUS installations have been updated (effective Sept 4, 
2024).  This will affect existing OCONUS RFP's and designs according to UFC 1-200-01 
(Chapter 1-3.1). 
Reason for changes: 
Seismic acceleration coefficients (earthquake loading) for OCONUS installations have 
not been fully updated since the 1990's. At that time, they were prepared based on less 
reliable information.  In 2010, the Global Earthquake Model (GEM), a non-profit 
foundation, began a multi-year effort to construct a global earthquake hazard model 
using high quality site hazard data available from governments, academia, and industry 
resources.  This Model is continuously refined and improved. In 2021, the Department 
of Defense (DoD), in partnership with the Department of State (DoS), contracted with 
GEM to develop new seismic design values for all OCONUS DoD installations and DoS 
facilities using the GEM model.  Results from this effort have recently become available 
and have been incorporated into DoD design criteria (effective Sept 4, 2024).  
Impact: 
There may be a significant cost increase for some locations.  Because prior values were 
based on less reliable information, this update has resulted in numerous changes.  In 
most cases changes are mild to moderate. However, in a few locations, values have 
increased markedly.  For this reason, this change has the potential to result in a 
significant cost increase for some locations.

Impact: 
There is no significant impact associated with this change.

Section 01 33 00 - Submittal Procedures
Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · issued for construction · 14 August 2026
1.1 Summary
This section governs the form of delegated-design submittals.
1.2 Units
Feet and inches, kips and pounds. Distributed loads and diaphragm unit shears in pounds per linear foot (plf);
concentrated forces and reactions in kips; deflections in inches; costs in United States dollars.
1.3 Coordinates
Plan coordinates are on the building grid with its origin at the south-west building corner, X positive east, Y positive
north, in feet.
1.4 Transmittal
One compressed archive per submittal.
1.5 Schedules
Schedules are delivered as a single workbook, one worksheet per schedule, the first row of each worksheet being the
column headings named in the design criteria and in the issued templates. Every row is complete: a cell left blank, or
filled with a placeholder such as TBD or N/A, makes the schedule incomplete and it is returned.
1.6 Calculation package and design basis
Calculations are delivered as one PDF on 8-1/2 x 11 portrait sheets covering the sections the design criteria lists, with a
separate design basis narrative in Markdown. The design basis carries a table of the values the design was built

--- Page 1 ---
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 1
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 — Structural Design Criteria: Roof Diaphragm and
Perimeter Shear Walls
Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · Lewis and Clark County, Montana · Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC · Revision 2, 14
August 2026 · supersedes Revision 0 of 3 May 2024
1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
collector forces, deflections - is an ALLOWABLE STRESS DESIGN quantity, obtained from the strength-level
wind effect by the load combination 0.6W. Member and connection capacities are compared against it on the
same basis. The drawings and the calculation package must state on their face that the loads shown are ASD.
4. Wind parameters
4.1 Exposure Category C, open terrain, in all directions. Enclosure classification: enclosed, GCpi = ±0.18. Internal
pressure acts on opposite internal faces simultaneously and therefore cancels in the net lateral force on the main wind
force resisting system; it is not to be included in the diaphragm and shear wall loads. It is included in the out-of-plane
panel design, which is a separate submittal.
4.2 The velocity pressure at elevation z is
    q(z) = 0.00256 * Kz(z) * Kzt * Kd * Ke * V^2      [psf, V in mph]
    Kz(z) = 2.01 * (z / 900)^(2/9.5),  z not taken less than 15 ft
with Kd = 0.85 and V from the AHJ letter. q_h is q(z) evaluated at the mean roof height; the velocity pressure for a
parapet is evaluated at the top of that parapet.
4.3 The topographic factor Kzt is taken from the site-specific study TS-2026-02 and applies over the whole footprint.
Revision 0 of this criteria carried Kzt = 1.00 and a basic wind speed of 105 mph; both were superseded when
the topographic study and the AHJ letter were issued.
4.4 The ground elevation factor is
    Ke = exp(-0.0000362 * zg)      zg = site ground elevation above sea level, ft
with zg taken from the ALTA survey benchmark. Ke is not to be taken as 1.0 at this site.

The wall lines are identified S (south, y = 0), E (east, x = 240), N1 (north, y = 180), W (west, x = 0), and, on the
generator yard, N2 (y = 140) and E2 (x = 180).
5. Precast wall panels
5.1 The perimeter walls are precast concrete panels spanning vertically between the foundation and the roof deck, with
a parapet cantilevering above the deck. Panel-to-panel joints transfer no in-plane shear: each panel resists in-plane
force independently.
5.2 Panel concrete f'c = 5000 psi, Ec = 4030 ksi, G = 0.40 Ec, unit weight 150 pcf.
5.3 Panel geometry - mark, length, thickness, top elevation and openings - is taken from the as-built federated model
and the roof line scan. Where the 2024 precast panel schedule and the as-built model disagree, the as-built model
governs and the difference is to be reported in the design basis.
5.4 Openings divide a panel into vertical legs. A leg is the full-height strip of panel between an opening edge and the
next opening edge or panel edge. A leg narrower than 2.0 ft is neglected: it is assigned no stiffness and carries no
in-plane shear.
5.5 Each leg is idealised as a cantilever pier fixed at the foundation and free at the roof deck, of height h equal to the
roof deck elevation, with
    k = 1 / ( h^3 / (3 Ec I) + 1.2 h / (G A) )        [kip/in]
    I = t L^3 / 12,   A = t L,   t = panel thickness, L = leg length
with h, t and L in inches. The parapet above the deck contributes no in-plane stiffness.
5.6 A panel's in-plane shear is the sum of the shears of its legs.
5.7 The panel base connection to the foundation has the ASD shear capacity per foot of panel length given in the
connection vendor data; the demand is the panel's in-plane shear.
5.8 Panel stability is checked with the ASD combination 0.6D + 0.6W: the overturning moment is the panel's ASD
in-plane shear times the roof deck elevation, and the resisting moment is 0.6 times the panel self weight times half the
panel length. Where the resisting moment is insufficient, a base tie-down assembly is provided; the assembly's ASD
capacity acts at a lever arm equal to the panel length. Panel self weight is computed on the GROSS panel area - full
panel length by top elevation by thickness - with no deduction for openings.
6. Wind pressures and the roof-level wall line load
6.1 The wind study reports a pressure coefficient for each facade patch and each azimuth, referenced to q_h. The
design pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp. The net pressure on a parapet patch is p = q_p * GCpn, with q_p the

--- Page 3 ---
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 3
velocity pressure at the top of that parapet and GCpn the study's net parapet coefficient; the parapet coefficient already
includes both faces.
6.2 Patch geometry is not tabulated in the wind study. A patch covers the full length of the panel it names and the
elevation band its identifier names; the bands are defined in the wind study. Panel lengths and top elevations come
from the as-built model.
6.3 Wall pressures act on the gross wall area, including door and louver openings; the door and louver framing delivers
its reaction to the surrounding panel.
6.4 Each panel spans vertically as a simple beam between the foundation and the roof deck. A patch pressure
p acting on an area A whose centroid is at elevation z therefore delivers
    R_roof = p * A * z / h        to the roof deck, and
    R_base = p * A * (1 - z/h)    to the foundation
with h the roof deck elevation. A patch above the deck - a parapet or a screen wall - has z > h, so it delivers
MORE than its own force to the diaphragm and an uplift-sense reaction at the base: this is the lever action of
the wall cantilevering above the diaphragm and it is not to be omitted. The roof-level line load on a wall line is the
sum of R_roof over the patches of that line, per foot of wall.
6.5 The line load acts along the wall's inward normal.
6.6 Torsional case. For wind on either principal axis the diaphragm is also checked with all line loads factored by 0.75
together with a torsional moment
    M_T = e * B * |F|        e = +/- 0.15
where |F| is the magnitude of the factored resultant in the direction of the wind and B the horizontal building dimension
perpendicular to the wind (240 ft for wind on the north or south face, 180 ft for wind on the east or west face). M_T is
applied to the diaphragm as a set of in-plane nodal forces proportional to the nodal tributary area and to the distance
from the diaphragm area centroid, directed perpendicular to that radius, scaled so that their moment about the centroid
equals M_T.
7. Roof deck
7.1 The roof is divided into the deck zones shown on S-201. Exactly one deck type from the deck manufacturer's
catalogue is used over the whole of each zone.
7.2 The diaphragm unit shear anywhere within a zone must not exceed the ASD shear capacity of that zone's deck
type. The catalogue tabulates NOMINAL strengths; the safety factor for the ASD capacity is given in the catalogue's
notes.
7.3 The catalogue's shear stiffness G' is tabulated for the deck span stated in its notes; where the framing gives a
different deck span, the note's adjustment applies. The adjustment applies to stiffness only, never to strength.
8. Acceptance limits
8.1 All checks are on the ASD basis of 3.3.
8.2 Diaphragm deflection. For each scenario and each global axis, the deflection of the diaphragm relative to its
supports is the largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from the stiffness-weighted mean displacement of the
piers that resist that axis. It must not exceed 0.55 in, the value the Owner's Basis of Design sets for the precast
connection detail.
8.3 Pier drift must not exceed h / 400.
9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this build

To hold the erection, inspection and quality-assurance programme to one mobilisation per trade, not more than 4 distinct roof deck types (gauge, support fastener pattern and sidelap connection count taken together) may be used across the Building A2 roof.

WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

--- Page 2 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.

TS-2026-02 — Site-Specific Topographic Wind Study
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · 30 April 2026 · Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2
1. Setting
The campus occupies a bench on the west side of the valley. The ground rises about 190 ft over roughly 1,500 ft from
the valley floor to the bench, and the parcel sits within the upper quarter of that rise.
2. Feature classification
The feature is an escarpment for winds from the east through south-east and a two-dimensional ridge for winds from
the west. The escarpment case governs.
3. Method
Speed-up was evaluated from the measured terrain profile along sixteen radials and checked against the model study's
approach flow.
4. Result
The topographic factor to be applied over the whole Building A2 footprint, at all elevations and for all azimuths,
is Kzt = 1.19. No reduction with height is taken within the height of this building.
5. Note on earlier work
The 2024 preliminary structural criteria took Kzt = 1.00 pending this study. That value is superseded.

            for bname, (bh, bz) in bands.items(): R += qh * cp_data[az][f"{mark}-{bname}"] * (L * bh) * (bz / 28.0)
            ph = top_z - 28.0; pz = 0.5 * (top_z + 28.0)
            R += q(top_z) * cp_data[az][f"{mark}-P"] * (L * ph) * (pz / 28.0)
            R_asd = 0.6 * R / 1000.0; line_tot[line] += R_asd; line_len[line] += L
        for line, (s_start, s_end) in line_extents.items():
            axis, fixed_coord, pier_dof, inward_sign = line_geom[line]
            load_dof = 1 - pier_dof
            w_avg = factor * line_tot[line] / line_len[line]
            line_loads_plf[(sc_id, line)] = abs(w_avg) * 1000.0
            n_seg = int(round((s_end - s_start) / H))
            for iseg in range(n_seg):
                sa = s_start + iseg * H; sb = sa + H
                if axis == "x":
                    n1 = grid_to_node[(int(round(sa/H)), int(round(fixed_coord/H)))]
                    n2 = grid_to_node[(int(round(sb/H)), int(round(fixed_coord/H)))]
                else:
                    n1 = grid_to_node[(int(round(fixed_coord/H)), int(round(sa/H)))]
                    n2 = grid_to_node[(int(round(fixed_coord/H)), int(round(sb/H)))]
                F_mat[2*n1 + load_dof, s_idx] += inward_sign * w_avg * H / 2.0
                F_mat[2*n2 + load_dof, s_idx] += inward_sign * w_avg * H / 2.0
        if ecc != 0.0:
            F_res = float(abs(np.sum(F_mat[wind_dof::2, s_idx])))
            MT = ecc * B_dim * F_res
            F_mat[0::2, s_idx] += -MT * nodal_area * dy_arr / J_polar
            F_mat[1::2, s_idx] += +MT * nodal_area * dx_arr / J_polar
    u_mat = spla.spsolve(K_csr, F_mat)
    return cells, grid_to_node, node_coords, pier_nodes, chord_segs, line_loads_plf, u_mat

# Self-check assert: verify violated-constraint failure on weak design (all D22-36/4-2 and PL3x3/8)
weak_gp = {z: 17.8 * (1.15 if z == "Z22" else 1.0) for z in zone_sel}
weak_cA = {c: 1.125 for c in chord_order}
_, _, _, _, _, _, u_weak = run_mesh(5.0, weak_gp, weak_cA)
assert float(np.max(np.abs(u_weak)) * 12.0) > 0.55, "Expected weak design to violate 0.55 in deflection limit"

# Run L1, L2, L3 on optimal design
conv_rows = []
for lvl, H in [("L1", 10.0), ("L2", 5.0), ("L3", 2.50)]:
    cells, grid_to_node, node_coords, pier_nodes, chord_segs, line_loads_plf, u_mat = run_mesh(H)
    reac_W_W01 = abs(sum(k_ft * u_mat[2*n + dof_dir, 0] for pid, mark, line, n, dof_dir, k_ft in pier_nodes if line == "W"))
    dN_dx_c = 0.25 * np.array([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, -1.0]) * (2.0 / H)
    dN_dy_c = 0.25 * np.array([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0]) * (2.0 / H)
    max_v_W01 = 0.0
    for ix, iy, xc, yc, zid, cnodes in cells:
        Ghat = 12.0 * zone_gp_used[zid]
        ue = u_mat[[2*n for n in cnodes], 0]
        ve = u_mat[[2*n+1 for n in cnodes], 0]
        v_plf = float(abs(Ghat * (dN_dy_c @ ue + dN_dx_c @ ve)) * 1000.0)
        if v_plf > max_v_W01: max_v_W01 = v_plf
    conv_rows.append((lvl, H, len(cells), round(max_v_W01, 2), round(reac_W_W01, 4)))
    if lvl == "L2":
        prod_data = (cells, grid_to_node, node_coords, pier_nodes, chord_segs, line_loads_plf, u_mat)

# Self-check convergence <= 5%
conv_diff_pct = abs(conv_rows[1][4] - conv_rows[2][4]) / conv_rows[2][4] * 100.0
assert conv_diff_pct <= 5.0, f"Convergence {conv_diff_pct}% > 5.0%"

cells, grid_to_node, node_coords, pier_nodes, chord_segs, line_loads_plf, u_mat = prod_data
H = 5.0
dN_dx_c = 0.25 * np.array([-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, -1.0]) * (2.0 / H)
dN_dy_c = 0.25 * np.array([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0]) * (2.0 / H)

# Pier embeds and tiedowns
panel_max_V = defaultdict(float)
for pid, mark, line, n, dof_dir, k_ft in pier_nodes:
    V_max = float(np.max(np.abs(k_ft * u_mat[2*n + dof_dir, :])))
    panel_max_V[mark] += V_max

panel_embeds = {}
panel_tiedown = {}
for mark, (line, s0, s1, L, t_in, top_z) in panels.items():
    V_req = panel_max_V[mark]
    assert V_req <= 1.40 * L, f"Panel {mark} base shear {V_req} exceeds B1 capacity {1.40*L}"
    n_min_sp = math.ceil(L / 8.0 - 1e-9)
    n_min_sh = math.ceil(V_req / 4.20 - 1e-9)
    n_emb = max(2, n_min_sp, n_min_sh)
    panel_embeds[mark] = n_emb
    w_dl_kip_ft = (t_in / 12.0) * 0.150 * top_z
    M_OT = V_req * 28.0
    M_R = 0.6 * (w_dl_kip_ft * L) * (L / 2.0)
    if M_OT > M_R:
        assert M_OT <= M_R + 88.0 * L, f"Panel {mark} overturning exceeds T1 capacity"
        panel_tiedown[mark] = "yes"
    else:
        panel_tiedown[mark] = "no"

# Zone peak shears check
zone_peak_v = defaultdict(float)
for ix, iy, xc, yc, zid, cnodes in cells:
    Ghat = 12.0 * zone_gp_used[zid]
    ue = u_mat[[2*n for n in cnodes], :]
    ve = u_mat[[2*n+1 for n in cnodes], :]
    v_max = float(np.max(np.abs(Ghat * (dN_dy_c @ ue + dN_dx_c @ ve))) * 1000.0)
    if v_max > zone_peak_v[zid]: zone_peak_v[zid] = v_max
for zid, (dcode, area, mult) in zone_sel.items():
    assert zone_peak_v[zid] <= deck_cat[dcode][1], f"Zone {zid} shear {zone_peak_v[zid]} > {deck_cat[dcode][1]}"

# Build workbook lateral_schedule.xlsx
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("templates/lateral_schedule_template.xlsx")

# 1. DeckZones
ws = wb["DeckZones"]
z_order = ["Z11", "Z12", "Z13", "Z21", "Z22", "Z23", "Z31", "Z32", "Z33", "Z41", "Z42", "Z43"]
deck_rows = []
for r_idx, zid in enumerate(z_order, start=2):
    dcode, area, mult = zone_sel[zid]
    gp0, cap, ucost, vnom = deck_cat[dcode]
    gp_used = round(gp0 * mult, 2)
    cap_r = round(cap, 2)
    cost_r = round(area * ucost, 2)
    row_vals = [zid, dcode, gp_used, cap_r, area, cost_r]
    deck_rows.append(row_vals)
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
        ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)

# 2. ChordSchedule
ws = wb["ChordSchedule"]
chord_sched_rows = []
for r_idx, cid in enumerate(chord_order, start=2):
    x0, y0, x1, y1, L_c, scode = chord_defs[cid]
    A_c, wt_plf, T_all, C_all = chord_cat[scode]
    cost_c = round(wt_plf * L_c * 2.85, 2)
    row_vals = [cid, scode, L_c, cost_c]
    chord_sched_rows.append(row_vals)
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
        ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)

# 3. Piers
ws = wb["Piers"]
pier_rows = []
for r_idx, (pid, mark, line, a, b, L_ft, t_in, top_ft, k_kip_in, mid) in enumerate(piers, start=2):
    row_vals = [pid, mark, line, round(a, 2), round(b, 2), round(L_ft, 2), round(t_in, 2), round(top_ft, 2), round(k_kip_in, 2), panel_embeds[mark], panel_tiedown[mark]]
    pier_rows.append(row_vals)
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
        ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)

# 4. ShearWalls
ws = wb["ShearWalls"]
sw_lines = ["S", "N1", "N2", "W", "E", "E2"]
sw_rows = []
r_idx = 2
for s_idx, (sc_id, az, factor, ecc, B_dim, wind_dof) in enumerate(scenarios):
    for line in sw_lines:
        ll_plf = round(line_loads_plf[(sc_id, line)], 2)
        reac = abs(sum(k_ft * u_mat[2*n + dof_dir, s_idx] for pid, mark, l_p, n, dof_dir, k_ft in pier_nodes if l_p == line))
        reac_r = round(reac, 3)
        row_vals = [sc_id, line, ll_plf, reac_r]
        sw_rows.append(row_vals)
        for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
            ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)
        r_idx += 1

# 5. Diaphragm
ws = wb["Diaphragm"]
diaph_rows = []
r_idx = 2
for s_idx, (sc_id, az, factor, ecc, B_dim, wind_dof) in enumerate(scenarios):
    for line in sw_lines:
        s_start, s_end = line_extents[line]
        L_line = s_end - s_start
        axis, fixed_coord, _, _ = line_geom[line]
        for frac in [0.25, 0.50, 0.75]:
            s_q = s_start + frac * L_line
            best_c = None; best_d = 1e9
            for idx_c, (ix, iy, xc, yc, zid, cnodes) in enumerate(cells):
                if axis == "x" and abs(yc - (fixed_coord + (2.5 if fixed_coord==0 else -2.5))) < 1e-6:
                    d = abs(xc - s_q)
                    if d < best_d: best_d = d; best_c = idx_c
                elif axis == "y" and abs(xc - (fixed_coord + (2.5 if fixed_coord==0 else -2.5))) < 1e-6:
                    d = abs(yc - s_q)
                    if d < best_d: best_d = d; best_c = idx_c
            ix, iy, xc, yc, zid, cnodes = cells[best_c]
            Ghat = 12.0 * zone_gp_used[zid]
            ue = u_mat[[2*n for n in cnodes], s_idx]
            ve = u_mat[[2*n+1 for n in cnodes], s_idx]
            v_plf = round(float(abs(Ghat * (dN_dy_c @ ue + dN_dx_c @ ve)) * 1000.0), 2)
            row_vals = [sc_id, line, frac, v_plf]
            diaph_rows.append(row_vals)
            for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
                ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)
            r_idx += 1

# 6. Chords
ws = wb["Chords"]
chord_force_rows = []
r_idx = 2
for s_idx, (sc_id, az, factor, ecc, B_dim, wind_dof) in enumerate(scenarios):
    for cid in chord_order:
        segs = chord_segs[cid]
        f_max = max(abs(k_bar * (u_mat[d2, s_idx] - u_mat[d1, s_idx])) for d1, d2, k_bar in segs)
        f_r = round(float(f_max), 3)
        assert f_r <= chord_cat[chord_defs[cid][5]][3], f"Chord {cid} force {f_r} exceeds compression allowable"
        row_vals = [sc_id, cid, f_r]
        chord_force_rows.append(row_vals)
        for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
            ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)
        r_idx += 1

# 7. Drift (Criteria 8.2: largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from stiffness-weighted mean displacement of piers resisting that axis)
ws = wb["Drift"]
drift_rows = []
kx_tot = sum(k_ft for _, _, _, n, d, k_ft in pier_nodes if d == 0)
ky_tot = sum(k_ft for _, _, _, n, d, k_ft in pier_nodes if d == 1)
r_idx = 2
for s_idx, (sc_id, az, factor, ecc, B_dim, wind_dof) in enumerate(scenarios):
    ux = u_mat[0::2, s_idx] * 12.0
    uy = u_mat[1::2, s_idx] * 12.0
    ux_bar = sum(k_ft * (u_mat[2*n, s_idx]*12.0) for _, _, _, n, d, k_ft in pier_nodes if d == 0) / kx_tot
    uy_bar = sum(k_ft * (u_mat[2*n+1, s_idx]*12.0) for _, _, _, n, d, k_ft in pier_nodes if d == 1) / ky_tot
    ux_rel = round(float(np.max(np.abs(ux - ux_bar))), 4)
    uy_rel = round(float(np.max(np.abs(uy - uy_bar))), 4)
    assert ux_rel <= 0.55 and uy_rel <= 0.55, f"Deflection {ux_rel}/{uy_rel} > 0.55 in"
    for d_axis, d_val in [("X", ux_rel), ("Y", uy_rel)]:
        row_vals = [sc_id, d_axis, d_val]
        drift_rows.append(row_vals)
        for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
            ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)
        r_idx += 1

# 8. Convergence
ws = wb["Convergence"]
for r_idx, row_vals in enumerate(conv_rows, start=2):
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
        ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)

# 9. Cost
ws = wb["Cost"]
deck_305_area = sum(a for z, (dc, a, m) in zone_sel.items() if dc == "D22-36/4-2")
deck_334_area = sum(a for z, (dc, a, m) in zone_sel.items() if dc == "D22-36/4-4")
deck_395_area = sum(a for z, (dc, a, m) in zone_sel.items() if dc == "D22-36/7-4")
deck_443_area = sum(a for z, (dc, a, m) in zone_sel.items() if dc == "D20-36/7-4")
steel_lbs = round(sum(chord_cat[cdef[5]][1] * cdef[4] for cdef in chord_defs.values()), 2)
tot_embeds = sum(panel_embeds.values())
tot_tiedowns = sum(1 for v in panel_tiedown.values() if v == "yes")

cost_rows = [
    ["Roof Deck D22-36/4-2 (SF)", deck_305_area, 3.05, round(deck_305_area * 3.05, 2)],
    ["Roof Deck D22-36/4-4 (SF)", deck_334_area, 3.34, round(deck_334_area * 3.34, 2)],
    ["Roof Deck D22-36/7-4 (SF)", deck_395_area, 3.95, round(deck_395_area * 3.95, 2)],
    ["Roof Deck D20-36/7-4 (SF)", deck_443_area, 4.43, round(deck_443_area * 4.43, 2)],
    ["Chord and Collector Steel (lb)", steel_lbs, 2.85, round(steel_lbs * 2.85, 2)],
    ["Deck-to-Panel Shear Embeds E1 (ea)", tot_embeds, 185.00, round(tot_embeds * 185.00, 2)],
    ["Panel Base Tie-Downs T1 (ea)", tot_tiedowns, 2450.00, round(tot_tiedowns * 2450.00, 2)],
]
for r_idx, row_vals in enumerate(cost_rows, start=2):
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row_vals, start=1):
        ws.cell(r_idx, c_idx, val)

total_cost_usd = round(sum(r[3] for r in cost_rows), 2)
assert total_cost_usd <= 310000.0, f"Cost {total_cost_usd} > 310000"

wb.save("output/lateral_schedule.xlsx")

# Compute governing scenario per wall line (by shear wall reaction, and also check by line load)
gov_by_reac = {}
gov_by_ll = {}
for line in sw_lines:
    best_sc_r = max([r for r in sw_rows if r[1] == line], key=lambda x: x[3])
    best_sc_l = max([r for r in sw_rows if r[1] == line], key=lambda x: x[2])
    gov_by_reac[line] = (best_sc_r[0], best_sc_r[3], best_sc_r[2])
    gov_by_ll[line] = (best_sc_l[0], best_sc_l[2], best_sc_l[3])

facts = {
    "total_cost_usd": total_cost_usd,
    "deck_cost_usd": round(sum(r[5] for r in deck_rows), 2),
    "chord_cost_usd": round(sum(r[3] for r in chord_sched_rows), 2),
    "steel_lbs": steel_lbs,
    "embed_count": tot_embeds,
    "embed_cost_usd": round(tot_embeds * 185.00, 2),
    "tiedown_count": tot_tiedowns,
    "tiedown_cost_usd": round(tot_tiedowns * 2450.00, 2),
    "tiedown_panels": sorted([m for m, v in panel_tiedown.items() if v == "yes"]),
    "zone_peak_v": {z: round(v, 2) for z, v in zone_peak_v.items()},
    "panel_max_V": {m: round(v, 3) for m, v in panel_max_V.items()},
    "gov_by_reac": gov_by_reac,
    "gov_by_ll": gov_by_ll,
    "convergence": conv_rows,
    "deck_rows": deck_rows,
    "chord_sched_rows": chord_sched_rows,
    "pier_rows": pier_rows,
    "sw_rows": sw_rows,
    "diaph_rows": diaph_rows,
    "chord_force_rows": chord_force_rows,
    "drift_rows": drift_rows,
    "cost_rows": cost_rows,
}
with open("/tmp/.ple_work_246d1e723d0b/facts.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(facts, f, indent=2)

print("Saved output/lateral_schedule.xlsx and facts.json successfully. Total cost:", facts["total_cost_usd"])
print("Governing scenario by reaction:", gov_by_reac)
print("Governing scenario by line load:", gov_by_ll)

## 4. Resolution of Conflicts Between Issued Documents

Every discrepancy between the 2023–2024 preliminary/fabrication documents and the 2026 as-built and governing documents was identified and resolved in accordance with Document Transmittal `T-204` and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2:

1. **Structural Design Criteria Revision 2 (`2026-08-14`) vs. Revision 0 (`2024-05-03`, Superseded) and AHJ Pre-Application Memorandum:**
   - *Conflict:* `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 (and the 2024 pre-application memorandum noted in `NDDC-AHJ-014` Section 4) specified Risk Category II, a basic wind speed of $V = 105\text{ mph}$, $K_{zt} = 1.00$, $K_e = 1.00$, precast concrete strength $f'_c = 4,000\text{ psi}$ ($E_c = 3,605\text{ ksi}$), pure flexural cantilever pier stiffness neglecting shear deformation, no parapet cantilever lever action above the roof deck, and a simple flexible-diaphragm tributary analysis.
   - *Resolution:* Per `T-204` Item 12 and `NDDC-AHJ-014` Sections 2–4, Rev 0 is superseded and archived. The design is governed by `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 and `NDDC-AHJ-014`, which establish Risk Category III, $V = 115\text{ mph}$ (3-second gust), Exposure C, $K_d = 0.85$, $f'_c = 5,000\text{ psi}$ ($E_c = 4,030\text{ ksi}$, $G = 0.40 E_c = 1,612\text{ ksi}$), Timoshenko flexural-plus-shear cantilever pier stiffness, full parapet lever action ($z/h > 1$), and the `DIAPH-MT 1.0` 2D semi-rigid finite element procedure.

2. **Building A1 Lateral Study (`HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf`) vs. Building A2 Wind Tunnel Study (`WT-2026-07`):**
   - *Conflict:* The project archive contains `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf` (14 September 2023), which evaluated a $200\text{ ft} \times 160\text{ ft} \times 24\text{ ft}$ rectangular building with a $2\text{ ft}$ parapet at $V = 105\text{ mph}$, $q_h = 18.9\text{ psf}$, and uniform `D22-36/4-2` deck.
   - *Resolution:* As stated on the face of `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf` and `T-204` Item 15, that study is for Building A1 and is not applicable to Building A2. Building A2 is designed using the site-specific boundary-layer wind tunnel study `WT-2026-07` and pressure coefficient dataset `WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv`.

3. **Topographic Factor $K_{zt}$ and Ground Elevation Factor $K_e$ (`TS-2026-02` and `ALTA-2025-77` vs. 2024 Assumptions):**
   - *Conflict:* Earlier 2024 work assumed flat-terrain sea-level defaults $K_{zt} = 1.00$ and $K_e = 1.00$.
   - *Resolution:* Per `TS-2026-02` Section 4 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 4.3, the governing escarpment speed-up factor $K_{zt} = 1.19$ is applied over the entire Building A2 footprint at all elevations and azimuths. Per `ALTA-2025-77` Section 1 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 4.4, Building A2 finished floor is at $z_g = 3,940.0\text{ ft}$ NAVD 88 (referenced to benchmark `BM-2` at $3,941.02\text{ ft}$), giving $K_e = \exp(-0.0000362 \times 3940.0) = 0.8671$. ## 4. Resolution of Conflicts Between Issued Documents

   - *Resolution:* Per `T-204` Item 12 and `NDDC-AHJ-014` Sections 2–4, Rev 0 is superseded and archived. The design is governed by `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 and `NDDC-AHJ-014`, which establish Risk Category III, $V = 115	ext{ mph}$ (3-second gust), Exposure C, $K_d = 0.85$, $f'_c = 5,000	ext{ psi}$ ($E_c = 4,030	ext{ ksi}$, $G = 0.40 E_c = 1,612	ext{ ksi}$), Timoshenko flexural-plus-shear cantilever pier stiffness, full parapet lever action ($z/h > 1$), and the `DIAPH-MT 1.0` 2D semi-rigid finite element procedure.

2. **Building A1 Lateral Study (`HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf`) vs. Building A2 Wind Tunnel Study (`WT-2026-07`):**
   - *Conflict:* The project archive contains `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf` (14 September 2023), which evaluated a $200	ext{ ft} 	imes 160	ext{ ft} 	imes 24	ext{ ft}$ rectangular building with a $2	ext{ ft}$ parapet at $V = 105	ext{ mph}$, $q_h = 18.9	ext{ psf}$, and uniform `D22-36/4-2` deck.
   - *Resolution:* As stated on the face of `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023.pdf` and `T-204` Item 15, that study is for Building A1 and is not applicable to Building A2. Building A2 is designed using the site-specific boundary-layer wind tunnel study `WT-2026-07` and pressure coefficient dataset `WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv`.

3. **Topographic Factor $K_{zt}$ and Ground Elevation Factor $K_e$ (`TS-2026-02` and `ALTA-2025-77` vs. 2024 Assumptions):**
   - *Conflict:* Earlier 2024 work assumed flat-terrain sea-level defaults $K_{zt} = 1.00$ and $K_e = 1.00$.
   - *Resolution:* Per `TS-2026-02` Section 4 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 4.3, the governing escarpment speed-up factor $K_{zt} = 1.19$ is applied over the entire Building A2 footprint at all elevations and azimuths. Per `ALTA-2025-77` Section 1 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 4.4, Building A2 finished floor is at $z_g = 3,940.0	ext{ ft}$ NAVD 88 (referenced to benchmark `BM-2` at $3,941.02	ext{ ft}$), giving $K_e = \exp(-0.0000362 	imes 3940.0) = 0.8671$.    - *Conflict:* `A-101_Roof_Plan_RevA_SUPERSEDED.dxf` showed a simple $240	ext{ ft} 	imes 180	ext{ ft}$ ($43,200	ext{ sf}$) rectangle without a northeast generator yard notch.
   - *Resolution:* `A-101` Rev A is superseded per `T-204` Item 13.    - *Conflict:* The 2024 precast panel schedule (`PC-S01_Precast_Panel_Schedule_2024.xlsx`) lists all 63 perimeter panels with a uniform top-of-panel elevation of $+31.0	ext{ ft}$ ($3.0	ext{ ft}$ parapet above the $+28.0	ext{ ft}$ roof deck).

   - *Conflict:* `PC-S02_Precast_Panel_Elevations_Rev1_SUPERSEDED.dxf` showed a preliminary $6.0	ext{ ft} 	imes 8.0	ext{ ft}$ shop opening in panel `S14` ($x = 192.0$ to $204.0	ext{ ft}$) from $x = 196.0$ to $202.0	ext{ ft}$ that was deleted prior to fabrication in `PC-S01` (`openings_shown = none`) and `PC-S02` Rev 2.    - *Resolution:* Inspection of `NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc` reveals an as-built field-cut $8.0	ext{ ft}	ext{ wide} 	imes 12.0	ext{ ft}	ext{ high}$ opening (`S14-O1`) in panel `S14` extending from station $s_0 = 194.50	ext{ ft}$ to $s_1 = 202.50	ext{ ft}$ ($59,283.6	ext{ mm}$ to $61,722.0	ext{ mm}$). Per `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Sections 5.3 and 5.4, this opening divides panel `S14` ($192.00$ to $204.00	ext{ ft}$) into two vertical legs:
     - Left leg ($192.00$ to $194.50	ext{ ft}$): width $L = 2.50	ext{ ft} \ge 2.0	ext{ ft}$, retained as structural pier `S14` with thickness $t = 8.0	ext{ in}$ and Timoshenko stiffness $k = 6.32	ext{ kip/in}$ ($6.3186	ext{ kip/in}$).
     - Right leg ($202.50$ to $204.00	ext{ ft}$): width $L = 1.50	ext{ ft} < 2.0	ext{ ft}$, neglected per Section 5.4 (assigned zero stiffness and carries no in-plane shear).
     Thus, the 63 perimeter panels produce exactly 73 active structural shear wall piers across the six wall lines (`S`: 19 piers, `E`: 12 piers, `E2`: 4 piers, `N2`: 5 piers, `N1`: 15 piers, `W`: 18 piers; 73 total).

7. **Joist Spacing and Deck Span Stiffness Adjustment in Zone `Z22` (`SJ-201` Note 1 & Note 2 and `CDS-B36` Note 4):**
   - *Conflict:* `SJ-201` Note 1 states that joists run north-south at $5	ext{ ft } 0	ext{ in}$ o.c. typically while referring to the $6	ext{ ft } 0	ext{ in}$ standard deck span tabulated in `CDS-B36`, whereas `SJ-201` Note 2 specifies that in mechanical bay Zone `Z22` the joists are doubled to $4	ext{ ft } 0	ext{ in}$ o.c. (`deck span there is 4 ft 0 in`).
   - *Resolution:* Per `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Sections 7.3 and 9.2 and `CDS-B36` Note 4, the smeared framing axial rigidities are taken from the `SJ-201` schedule values ($EA_x = 29,000 	imes 4.0 / 40.0 = 2,900	ext{ kip/ft}$ and $EA_y = 29,000 	imes 2.4 / 5.0 = 13,920	ext{ kip/ft}$, matching Verification Example `VE-1`), while in Zone `Z22` the $4	ext{ ft } 0	ext{ in}$ deck span requires multiplying the catalogue shear stiffness $G'$ by `1.15` (so `D22-36/4-2` in `Z22` uses $G'_{	ext{used}} = 17.80 	imes 1.15 = 20.47	ext{ kip/in}$) with no change to its ASD shear capacity ($980 / 2.35 = 417.02	ext{ plf}$).

steps.message:
The lateral engineering package for **Building A2 at the Northern Divide Data Campus** (Lewis and Clark County, Montana) has been completed and packaged in `/filesystem/final_batch4__structural_task5_wind_diaphragm_shear__blind/output/submission.zip`, containing all five required files:

1. **`lateral_schedule.xlsx`** (in `output/submission.zip` and `output/lateral_schedule.xlsx`) — Nine worksheets matching `templates/lateral_schedule_template.xlsx`:
   - `DeckZones`: 12 roof deck zones (`Z11`–`Z43`, total net area $39,600.0\text{ sf}$, deducting the $60\text{ ft} \times 40\text{ ft}$ northeast generator yard notch and $40\text{ ft} \times 30\text{ ft}$ interior mechanical well Opening O1) using 4 distinct deck types (`D22-36/4-2`, `D22-36/4-4`, `D22-36/7-4`, `D20-36/7-4`, $\le 4$ permitted by `OBD-NDDC-A2` Section 4.6), with the $1.15\times$ shear stiffness factor applied in Zone `Z22` ($4\text{ ft } 0\text{ in}$ joist spacing per `SJ-201` Note 2 and `CDS-B36` Note 4).
   - `ChordSchedule`: 12 perimeter chord, notch collector, and opening collector lines (`C-S`, `C-N1`, `C-N2`, `C-E`, `C-E2`, `C-W`, `K-N2`, `K-E2`, `O-S`, `O-N`, `O-W`, `O-E`, $1,300.0\text{ lf}$ total, $5,675.80\text{ lb}$ @ $\$2.85/\text{lb}$) using `PL10x5/8` on re-entrant notch chord `C-E2` and `PL3x3/8` on the remaining 11 lines.
   - `Piers`: 73 active structural precast concrete shear wall piers across the 63 perimeter panels (`f'c = 5,000 psi`, $E_c = 4,030\text{ ksi}$, $G = 1,612\text{ ksi}$, Timoshenko flexural-plus-shear cantilever stiffness $k_p$ at $h = 28.00\text{ ft}$), incorporating the $+36.00\text{ ft}$ north mechanical screen wall (`N108`–`N111`, $x = 96.0$ to $168.0\text{ ft}$ on line `N1`), the as-built field-cut opening `S14-O1` ($s = 194.50$ to $202.50\text{ ft}$ in panel `S14`), and neglecting pier legs narrower than $2.0\text{ ft}$ (`S14` right leg $1.50\text{ ft}$ and `N103` left leg $1.00\text{ ft}$).
   - `ShearWalls`: ASD ($0.6\text{W}$) roof-level line loads (`line_load_plf`) and in-plane shear wall reactions (`reaction_kips`) across all 12 wind scenarios (`W01`–`W12`) and 6 exterior wall lines (`S, N1, N2, W, E, E2`).
   - `Diaphragm`: Quarter-point (`0.25, 0.50, 0.75`) ASD diaphragm unit shears (`unit_shear_plf`) along all 6 wall lines for all 12 scenarios from the Level `L2` ($H = 5.0\text{ ft}$, 1,584-element) `DIAPH-MT 1.0` finite element model.
   - `Chords`: Peak ASD axial forces (`force_kips`) in all 12 chord and collector lines across `W01`–`W12`.
   - `Drift`: Peak relative in-plane diaphragm deflections (`deflection_in`) in global axes `X` and `Y` across `W01`–`W12` (peak `0.5378 in <= 0.5500 in` limit in `W01` Y-direction).
   - `Convergence`: Three-level mesh refinement study (`L1` at $H = 10.0\text{ ft}$ with 396 elements, `L2` at $H = 5.0\text{ ft}$ with 1,584 elements, `L3` at $H = 2.5\text{ ft}$ with 6,336 elements), showing a `0.24% <= 5.0%` change in the key Wall Line `W` reaction in `W01` between `L2` ($47.2043\text{ kips}$) and `L3` ($47.3193\text{ kips}$).
   - `Cost`: Itemized installed package cost summing to **`$205,906.03`** ($\le \$310,000.00$ ceiling): `$141,780.00` roof deck + `$16,176.03` chord/collector steel + `$25,900.00` for 140 Type E1 embeds + `$22,050.00` for 9 Type T1 base tie-downs.

2. **`diaphragm_plan.dxf`** (in `output/submission.zip` and `output/diaphragm_plan.dxf`) — CAD plan drawings on the building grid in feet (`[0, 240] x [0, 180]`) across all required template layers (`S-GRID`, `S-DIAP-ZONE`, `S-CHRD`, `S-COLL`, `S-DIAP-SHEAR`, `S-WALL-REAC`, `S-ANNO-TEXT`), presenting both the `TRANSVERSE` (`W01`) and `LONGITUDINAL` (`W03`) wind plans and 12-scenario ASD design envelopes.

3. **`constraint_register.xlsx`** (in `output/submission.zip` and `output/constraint_register.xlsx`) — Worksheet `Register` containing 114 verified requirement rows covering the governing document corpus (`EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2, `NDDC-AHJ-014`, `OBD-NDDC-A2`, `Spec_01_33_00`, `T-204`, `ALTA-2025-77`, `SR-2026-118`, `NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`, `WT-2026-07`, `TS-2026-02`, `CDS-B36`, `KRS-CH`, `KRS-CN`, `A-101`, `A-301`, `S-201`, `SJ-201`, `PC-S02`, `UFC 3-301-01`, `29 CFR 1926.704`, and `29 CFR 1926.757`).

4. **`calculations.pdf`** (in `output/submission.zip` and `output/calculations.pdf`) — Six-page portrait calculation package documenting the design basis, as-built geometry take-off, velocity pressures ($q_h = 28.75\text{ psf}$, $q_p(31\text{ ft}) = 29.37\text{ psf}$, $q_p(36\text{ ft}) = 30.31\text{ psf}$), parapet cantilever lever action, 73-pier stiffness schedule, `DIAPH-MT 1.0` benchmark verification (`VE-1` reproduction within $< 0.15\%$), mesh convergence, deck/chord/connection design checks, drift verification, and cost schedule.

5. **`design_basis.md`** (in `output/submission.zip` and `output/design_basis.md`) — Design basis narrative carrying the required design parameter table, governing wind scenario table per wall line, document precedence table, and detailed prose resolutions of all conflicts between the 2023–2024 preliminary/superseded documents and the 2026 governing as-built documents.
